data: South Korea's spaceport: Naro-1 (2009-13) and the home-built Nuri rocket since 2021

South Korea's launch site on the coast of Goheung County, run by the Korea Aerospace Research Institute, with two pads, LC-1 and LC-2. The first Naro-1 flight on 25 August 2009 failed to reach orbit; Nuri reached orbit on 21 June 2022. Facts from Wikipedia (Naro Space Center, Naro-1, Nuri); coordinates are the Wikipedia site point, between LC-1 and LC-2.
Naro Space Center Space Science Museum (Korean) — KARI
South Korea launches research satellites on third Nuri flight — NASASpaceFlight

Naro Space Center stands on the south coast of South Korea, in Goheung County about 485 km south of Seoul, and is run by KARI. It has two pads. The Naro-1 rocket, with a Russian first stage, flew from LC-1 three times: the flights of 25 August 2009 and 10 June 2010 failed to reach orbit, and on 30 January 2013 the third put the STSAT-2C satellite into low orbit. On 28 November 2018 a Nuri test vehicle flew a 10-minute suborbital hop to qualify its KRE-075 engine. Nuri, the first orbital rocket designed and built entirely in South Korea, lifted off from LC-2 on 21 October 2021 and failed in its third stage. Its second flight, on 21 June 2022, reached a 700 km orbit, and further flights followed on 25 May 2023, 26 November 2025 and 7 October 2026, all from LC-2.
